title: Time integration method selector
overview: Selects the time-integration method stored in Ctrl::time_integral. The global solver dispatch maps MULTI_STAGE to RungeKutta, SIMPLE to Simple, and every other value to Lusgs. The context-aware Relaxation overload applies the same dispatch.
principle: This is a discrete algorithm-selection parameter, not a continuous physical coefficient. Its meaning is defined by the dispatch branches that consume the stored selector. Unsupported or unrecognized values currently follow the Lusgs fallback branch; this declaration does not redefine that compatibility behavior as input validation.
architecture: The value is read by Ctrl::Init, NsCtrl::Init, INsCtrl::Init, and TurbCtrl::Init. The shared TimeIntegral implementation owns the method dispatch. Euler resident-backend eligibility is a separate capability decision and must not be conflated with selecting the RungeKutta method.

proves: The four listed control initializers read the selector.
TimeIntegral::Init and the context-aware Relaxation overload dispatch MULTI_STAGE, SIMPLE, and fallback values as described.
does_not_prove: The selected method's temporal order or stability region.
That every solver configuration can use the resident Euler RungeKutta backend.
Numerical accuracy or physical validity of a particular case.

verification.scope: Source-backed dispatch declaration; source links are listed under Implementation. No test execution is implied.
Context-aware overload applies the same method dispatch; no test execution is implied.

examples.title: Time-integration method dispatch
examples.input: Assume the configured selector is MULTI_STAGE, SIMPLE, or an unrecognized value.
examples.calculation: TimeIntegral dispatch maps MULTI_STAGE to RungeKutta, SIMPLE to Simple, and all other values to Lusgs. The context-aware Relaxation overload follows the same dispatch.
examples.result: MULTI_STAGE selects the multi-stage path; SIMPLE selects the simple path; an unrecognized selector currently takes the Lusgs fallback.
examples.limitations: This describes the current dispatch behavior, not input validation, formal accuracy, stability, or eligibility for the separate resident Euler backend.

formulas.title: OneFLOW time-integration method dispatch
formulas.plain: D(m) = RungeKutta if m = MULTI_STAGE; Simple if m = SIMPLE; Lusgs otherwise
formulas.assumptions: Describes TimeIntegral::Init and context-aware TimeIntegral::Relaxation. MULTI_STAGE=1, LUSGS=2, SIMPLE=3 are declared in TimeIntegral.h. The fallback branch handles every value other than MULTI_STAGE and SIMPLE; it is not input validation.

symbols.notes: An integer selector, not a physical coefficient.

symbols.meaning: Selector constant (1) that chooses OneFLOW's RungeKutta path.
symbols.notes: This dispatch label does not establish formal RK order.
Do not confuse with the SIMPLE pressure-velocity algorithm used in incompressible CFD.

symbols.meaning: Declared selector constant (2) and method used by dispatch fallback.
symbols.notes: The final branch also handles all values other than MULTI_STAGE and SIMPLE; it does not validate that the input equals 2.
Integer selector read by solver control initializers.
Value 3; distinct from the SIMPLE pressure-velocity algorithm.

symbols.meaning: Named selector constant and fallback method.
symbols.notes: Value 2; unknown values also currently enter the fallback branch.

caveats: The selector chooses an implementation path; it does not establish temporal order, stability region, or accuracy.
The SIMPLE label here means OneFLOW's TimeIntegral::Simple method, not the SIMPLE pressure-velocity coupling algorithm.
Resident Euler backend eligibility is a separate capability gate inside the RungeKutta path.
The fallback branch is observed compatibility behavior, not a recommended way to accept invalid selector values.
